change.author: Gabe Villalobos

findings.title: `queued` default is set once, when the module is imported
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs a single time, when the class is defined. Every `AssignmentSource` built without an explicit `queued` (including every one from `from_integration`) then carries the worker process's import time, not the time the assignment was queued. The field is wrong from the start and will mislead anyone who later reads it for ordering or staleness. Use `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. `test_to_dict` only checks that `queued` is not None, so it cannot catch this.

findings.title: No test covers the deassign path when the source integration matches
findings.body: Only `assign` is tested with a matching `assignment_source`. `deassign` got the same new parameter and is called that way from `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:96-99), but no test checks that an inbound unassign skips outbound sync to the same integration. Nothing checks either that a *different* integration still gets the outbound sync, which is the other half of the claim in `should_sync`'s comment.

findings.title: `assignment_source` added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` but nothing passes it
findings.body: No caller in this PR passes `assignment_source` to `sync_status_outbound`, and subclasses already take `**kwargs`. So this signature change has no effect and suggests status-sync cycle prevention that doesn't exist yet. Either drop it or wire it through in the PR that uses it.

contracts.action: Inbound assign/deassign from an integration passes AssignmentSource; the outbound task skips the same integration
contracts.equivalent_path: Manual deassign in src/sentry/api/helpers/group_index/update.py:904 calls deassign without a source, so outbound sync still goes to all linked integrations
contracts.before_after: Before: an inbound change triggered outbound sync back to the source integration (a cycle). After: should_sync returns False when sync_source.integration_id == org_integration.integration_id (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390-391)
contracts.visible_effect: The external issue is not re-assigned/updated by Sentry echoing back the change
contracts.failure_mode: from_dict returns None on bad input (assignment_source.py:31-35), so the task falls back to old behavior (sync happens). Task kwargs are pickled (src/sentry/conf/server.py:739), so the datetime in to_dict serializes fine. All sync_assignee_outbound implementations accept **kwargs (jira, jira_server, vsts, example), so the new assignment_source kwarg does not raise

summary: The cycle-prevention wiring works: inbound assign and deassign tag the change with its source integration, and the outbound task skips that integration. The tag survives the task queue because tasks are pickled, and every integration's `sync_assignee_outbound` accepts the new keyword argument. One thing to fix: `AssignmentSource.queued` defaults to the time the module was imported, not the time the assignment was queued. Two smaller points to consider: no test covers the deassign path or a different integration, and `sync_status_outbound` gained an `assignment_source` parameter that nothing passes.
